overview: This Senate resolution names October 4 through October 10, 2026, "National Community Policing Week." Community policing is an approach in which officers build relationships with the neighborhoods they serve and work with residents to solve safety problems. The resolution says this approach builds trust, protects both officers and civilians, and has helped reduce violent and property crime. It encourages the public, police agencies and elected officials to look for ways to improve safety and strengthen relationships. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on September 23, 2026.
for: Supporters say recognizing community policing encourages the trust and cooperation between police and residents that make neighborhoods safer for everyone.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it changes no law and provides no new resources to police departments or communities.
